summary: Round 2. Checked 58 claims against the codebase, found 4 mirages (0 critical, 1 major, 3 minor). All three major findings from round 1 are resolved and re-verified: styles.css truncation now belongs to Task 6 (wave 2, sole owner of the file in that wave), the onSave -> saveSettings -> updateBoard chain changes entirely inside Task 8, and the tsc/.svelte gap is recorded as Decision 11 with component verify switched to build+scenarios. Every new empirical claim in Decisions 3, 4, 8, 10, 11 was reproduced exactly — including the counts 'twelve inline assertions', 'four document.querySelector calls', 'three source locations', 'nine test expectations'. The stale comment in boardLayoutUtils.ts is still unowned and is now actively contradicted by the shipped behavior — raised to major.

findings.claim: tech-spec Dependencies says: 'src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts — computeGroupClasses, reused unchanged', and Solution says '`computeGroupClasses` is already order-agnostic and needs no change'. No task lists this file under 'Files to modify' (Task 4 and Task 7 list it only under 'Files to read').
findings.reality: The function body is genuinely order-agnostic — it walks whatever array it is handed and pairs adjacent halves, confirmed by reading src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts lines 5-25. But lines 3-4 of that same file carry a comment that asserts the opposite and issues an instruction: '// ВАЖНО: зависит от фиксированного порядка групп.\n// При появлении настраиваемого порядка — переработать.' Configurable order is exactly what this feature introduces, so on the day the feature ships the file will contain a standing instruction to rework it, referencing a condition that has already come true. Round 1 flagged this as minor on the assumption it was merely stale; it is worse than stale — a dev-code-reviewer reading the file during Task 7 (which must read it) has a documented reason to block, and the next feature's code research will read the comment as a live constraint on the ordering mechanism.
findings.source: 0011-feat-group-customization-tech-spec.md, sections Solution and Dependencies; Task 4 and Task 7 file lists
findings.fix: Add `src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts` to Task 7's 'Files to modify' and instruct it to delete those two comment lines (no logic change). Task 7 is the only task in Wave 3 and already owns the ordering mechanism, so there is no wave conflict and no other task touches the file. Alternatively state explicitly in Dependencies that the comment is knowingly left in place and why — but leaving it silent, as now, is the one option that will cost review time.

findings.claim: Decision 4 says the pure title helper 'keeps the four call sites identical'; the Architecture 'Display sites' bullet enumerates GroupHeader, CollapsibleGroup, GroupSettingsPopup, EmptyState.
findings.reality: `$groupLabels[groupId]` is rendered at five places, not four: src/ui/GroupHeader.svelte:20, src/ui/CollapsibleGroup.svelte:53, src/ui/GroupSettingsPopup.svelte:26, and src/ui/BoardSettingsPopup.svelte:60 (the group row name in the board settings popup) — plus EmptyState, which resolves its own key rather than a label. The fifth site sits in Task 8, not Task 6, and the spec never says what happens to it. The E2E line 'the input shows it as a placeholder' implies the row's name becomes an input with the default label as placeholder, which would be consistent — but that is inference, and Task 8's 'Files to read' includes `groupTitle.ts`, which suggests the helper is used there too, making the count five.
findings.fix: State in Task 8's description whether the popup row uses the resolved title as the input placeholder via `groupTitle`, or keeps raw `$groupLabels`. Then either correct 'four call sites' to five in Decision 4, or say explicitly that the popup row is a placeholder, not a display site.

findings.claim: Decision 8: 'The tooling requirement is `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` (build tooling) intersected with `^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0` (package manager); 22.12 is the simplest floor that satisfies both.'
findings.reality: Both quoted ranges are exact — `node_modules/vite/package.json` engines is `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`, and npm 11.13.0 prints `^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0` on the current Node v18.19.1. The floor 22.12 is correct. Two imprecisions remain. (a) The `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` range belongs to **vite**, which enters the project only as a transitive dependency of vitest — the project's actual build tool is esbuild (`npm run build` -> `node esbuild.config.mjs`). Calling it 'build tooling' points a future reader at the wrong package. (b) A third constraint is not mentioned: `node_modules/vitest/package.json` engines is `^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0`, which excludes the 23.x line. An `engines` value of `>=22.12` therefore admits Node 23, where vitest itself declares incompatibility.
findings.fix: Reword to 'the test toolchain (vite, a vitest dependency) requires ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0; npm requires ^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0; vitest itself requires ^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0'. If the pin is written as a range rather than a floor, `>=22.12 <23 || >=24` matches all three; if a bare floor is preferred, note that 23.x is knowingly out of vitest's declared range.

findings.claim: Wave 1 runs Tasks 3, 4 and 5 in parallel; Tasks 4 and 5 verify with `npm test`, and both list `src/data/types.ts` under 'Files to read' while Task 3 modifies it in the same wave.
findings.reality: `Group` in src/data/types.ts has no `title` field today (lines 22-28) and `Board` has no `groupOrder` (lines 30-39) — Task 3 adds both. `npm test` runs the whole unit suite (`vitest run`, include `tests/unit/**/*.test.ts`), which includes `tests/unit/migration.test.ts` — the file Task 3 is rewriting in the same wave, and which currently carries nine `expect(result.version).toBe(7)` assertions that must all become 8. So Task 4 and Task 5, verifying concurrently, can see a red suite for reasons entirely outside their own change, and Task 5 cannot type-check at all if its helper signature takes a `Group` rather than a plain string.
findings.source: 0011-feat-group-customization-tech-spec.md, Wave 1 (Tasks 3, 4, 5) and Agent Verification Plan rows 3-5
findings.fix: Either state the helper signatures explicitly as primitives (`resolveGroupTitle(storedTitle: string, defaultLabel: string)`, `moveGroup(order: GroupId[], ...)`) so Tasks 4 and 5 carry no dependency on Task 3's type change, or narrow their verify to their own suites (`npx vitest run tests/unit/groupOrderUtils.test.ts`) instead of a bare `npm test`.
